newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher, Bancoquia rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher, Bancoquia rebounds.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mostly higher in a session dominated by demand for cement maker Cementos Argos and Bancoquia, a bank whose stock fell sharply Monday on wild market rumors.

Banco de Colombia erased some of its recent losses in Medellin, but it closed lower for the third consecutive day in Bogota. Medellin's .IBOMED general price index edged down a razor-thin 0.03 percent to end at 17,248.13 on a trading volume of nearly two billion pesos. Bogota's .IBB closed shed 0.31 percent, meanwhile, closing at 1,122.34 on above-average volume of about 4 billion pesos.

Bancoquia, financial arm of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, fell nearly 10 percent in Bogota on Monday on rumors its plans to sell a 51 percent stake to Spain's Banco Santander had somehow fallen apart.
It shot back up 7.14 percent on Tuesday, closing at 3,000 pesos per share in Bogota, even though there was no official denial of the rumors.
The rumors about Bancoquia were fueled by a deal involving Banco de Colombia, whose talks to form a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano collapsed Friday.

Colombia, whose stock is trading well below book value, has moved steadily lower since the merger fell through. It extended its losses in Bogota Tuesday, ending down 1.78 percent at 385 pesos per share. But it eked out a 1.05 percent gain in Medellin.
Argos, the top cement company belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, led gains by adding 3.40 percent in Bogota to end at 8,531 pesos per share.
Traders attributed the move to active foreign fund buying and talks of strong first-quarter results.
